rows: Sand Dunes, Carson Desert, Nevada
Timothy O'Sullivan traveled with government surveyors across the deserts of the West. Here a wagon team crosses the sand dunes, tiny beside the hills of sand.
How would you cross a desert like this?
Yosemite Falls
Long before his famous horse pictures, Eadweard Muybridge photographed Yosemite under the Greek name "Helios," which means the Sun. His pictures of the tall waterfall made people dream of visiting.
How tall do you think the falls are compared with the trees?
The Angel at the Sepulchre
Julia Margaret Cameron staged scenes from the Bible and legends, using friends and neighbors as models. Soft focus and dramatic light make this picture of an angel feel like a painting.
Which parts of the picture look blurry, and why might Cameron want that?
A Study of Beatrice Cenci
Cameron borrowed the look of a famous Italian painting of Beatrice Cenci for this portrait. A young woman looks out from under a headcloth, with her eyes soft and thoughtful.
Do you think the woman looks happy, sad or both?
The Balloon Le Neptune, Montmartre

In the fall of 1870, Paris was surrounded by an enemy army. The city sent mail out by balloon, and Le Neptune lifted off from Montmartre on September 23. Nadar, the balloonist and photographer, organized balloon flights during the siege.
What would you put in a balloon mailbag?
Alexandre Dumas
Alexandre Dumas wrote adventures such as The Three Musketeers and The Count of Monte Cristo. Étienne Carjat photographed him in a studio portrait showing his curly hair and generous smile.
Which Dumas story would you most like to read?
Old Faithful

In 1871 William Henry Jackson joined an expedition to Yellowstone and photographed its geysers. The next year Congress made Yellowstone the first national park, and photographs like this helped persuade lawmakers.
What do you think the geyser sounds like?
The Paris Fire, Hôtel de Ville
In May 1871, during the Paris Commune uprising, fires destroyed the city hall of Paris. Charles Soulier photographed the empty, burned shell of the building.
Why would people want to remember a burned building?
Charles Darwin
Oscar Rejlander photographed Charles Darwin, the scientist who explained evolution, seated in profile with his big white beard. Rejlander also took photographs for Darwin's book about emotions.
What do you think Darwin is thinking about?
Valley of the Yosemite from Rocky Ford
Muybridge photographed Yosemite's cliffs and the Merced River in the 1870s. The mirrored water makes the valley seem twice as big.
What do you notice in the reflections?
Expressions of the Emotions

Charles Darwin used photographs by Oscar Rejlander in his 1872 book about how people and animals show feelings. These faces show laughing, crying and surprise. It was one of the first science books to use photographs.
Make each face yourself. Which emotions are easiest to show?
Ancient Ruins in the Cañon de Chelly

Timothy O'Sullivan photographed a stone house tucked in a canyon wall in Arizona, built about 800 years ago by the ancestors of the Pueblo people. He lowered himself on ropes and used long exposures to catch it.
Why would people build homes high up in a cliff?
Inscription Rock, El Morro

El Morro in New Mexico is a rock where travelers carved their names for hundreds of years, from Spanish explorers to settlers. O'Sullivan laid a ruler against the rock to show the size of the inscriptions.
Where would you carve your name, and what would you write?
Two Women of Ceylon
Julia Margaret Cameron moved with her husband to Ceylon (now Sri Lanka) in 1875. Her photographs there show women standing close together in the shade, one balancing a pot.
What do you think they were carrying?
Caney the Clown

John Thomson photographed the people who worked on London's streets, from clowns to chimney sweeps, for his book Street Life in London. It is one of the first books to show ordinary working people in photographs.
What kind of job is it to be a street clown?
